name: divisibility_constraint_set

phase_0.boundary_condition: The set of natural numbers N

VINIT.justification: The state before any numerical value or relation is defined.

TANCH.justification: The operator that defines the limits of the divisibility check.

AFWD.justification: The forward transformation of a number into its quotient parts.

AREV.justification: The inverse operation that reconstructs the dividend from quotient and divisor.

CLINK.justification: The iterative process that composes the division algorithm.

IMSCRIB.justification: The number that returns itself under division, representing self-recognition.

FSPLIT.justification: Splits a number into a quotient and a remainder.

FFUSE.justification: Recombines quotient and remainder to recover the original dividend.

EVALT.justification: The state where the divisibility constraint is satisfied.

EVALF.justification: The state where the divisibility constraint is violated.

ENGAGR.justification: A state where divisibility is neither true nor false but undefined.

IFIX.justification: The permanent, irreversible decomposition of a number into its atomic parts.

phase_3.void_description: Undefined numerical space before value assignment
phase_3.both_description: Singularity where division by zero occurs

steps.domain_action: Initialize the numerical register to null
Define the dividend as a self-consistent identity
Apply the divisor as a transformation vector
Branch the dividend into quotient and remainder paths
Verify if the remainder path contains the value zero
Verify if the remainder path contains a non-zero value
Recombine the quotient and remainder to verify integrity
Chain the result to the next constraint in the set
Record the divisibility status in the permanent factor table
Close the operation within the bounds of the number system

phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: Order of operations defined by operator precedence

phase_6.post_cycle_state: Ordered set of factors and remainders
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The information content of the dividend is preserved through the division and reconstruction cycle.
